summary: Chapter 2 dramatizes Feuz uncovering the reused death-certificate formula and closing the net toward Stettler, but along the way it silently rewrites several load-bearing canon facts (the victim's name, Melchior's cause of death, Stettler's office, Berta's household, and the priest's identity), so as written it does not earn its place.

issues.fix_hint: Restore the victim's name to Klara Vogel; cut the invented forename 'Anna' and the invented maiden name 'geborene Aebi', which is not in canon and implies a kinship to Aebischer that does not exist.

issues.unit: drei Blätter, ein Protokoll, ein Sektionsbefund
issues.fix_hint: Cut the Sektionsbefund from Melchior's file; canon (t4) records that Feuz files the certificate without an autopsy.

issues.unit: die Zusammensetzung des Präparats, das man im Magen gefunden hatte
issues.fix_hint: Replace the poisoning finding with the canon formula 'Herzversagen, vermutlich beim Sturz', reused identically across both cases.
Call him Amtsarzt, as canon does, not Amtsstatthalter.

issues.unit: Zu Hause hatte Berta die Suppe schon aufgetragen
issues.fix_hint: Cut Berta serving soup and coffee in Feuz's home; canon places her only as Melchior's widow, with no relation to Feuz's household.

issues.unit: der Pfarrer stand in der Tür
issues.fix_hint: Name the priest as Rutz (or Pfarrer Rutz) so this figure explicitly resolves to the one priest canon records, rather than reading as a second, unnamed cleric distinct from the creditor introduced earlier in the chapter.

issues.unit: Feuz hatte in zwanzig Jahren keinen Amtsstatthalter seine Unterschrift unterstreichen sehen
issues.fix_hint: Cut the twenty-years-of-service claim; canon records Feuz as young, not a veteran of two decades.
